image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of a dark-shelled turtle walking on dry grass and dirt. The turtle has a high-domed, oval carapace that is dark brown/black with visible scute boundaries and some lighter speckling. The head is extended, showing a pointed snout and small lateral eye. The skin on the neck and visible limb is dark with yellowish mottling. One forelimb is visible, appearing stout with claws. The background consists of out-of-focus dry vegetation.

The surface appears relatively smooth between scute boundaries, suggesting an adult or a species variation where keels are absent/very faint.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin on the neck and leg is dark (brown/black) with yellowish patterns. The texture appears granular/scaly rather than smooth, fitting the 'rough, scaly' description.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible forelimb is short and stout. Claws are visible at the end of the digits. Webbing is difficult to confirm definitively due to the angle and grass, but the foot structure is consistent with a semi-aquatic turtle.
The tail is located at the posterior end of the turtle and is completely occluded by the carapace and the angle of the shot. It is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a behavioral/anatomical capability that cannot be verified from a static image of an extended turtle. While the head is out, we cannot determine if it *can* retract fully without seeing the plastron size or observing movement.
